text:
Victor Olofsson's second stint in Vegas has started like a dream: 8 goals and 13 points in 13 games, and a seat next to Mark Stone when Stone set up the goal that made him the franchise's career points leader on Nov. 20, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted. He played once in early October, then came back in November and has seen his ice time climb by two minutes a night.

Our numbers say part of it is earned. His chances are up (3.4 expected goals on his own shots over the last ten games, against 2.7 usual), and Vegas takes 64% of the expected goals at five on five with him on. Six of his points have come on the power play.

The other part is a shooting percentage that can't last. He's at 28% after 9% last season, nearly four goals above what his chances deserve, and his points pace is far above our talent range of 1.76 to 2.61 per 60.

A seventh-round pick who has bounced between four teams has found the right linemates. The finish will come back to earth; the chances are the part to judge him on.
headline: Olofsson is back in Vegas and scoring
